correctness.rationale: Let primes p<q<r. At r only pq can witness, so pq-1=kr with 1<=k<=p-1. At q, witness r would force q|k+1 while 2<=k+1<=p<q, so pr must witness and q|k+p; bounds p<k+p<2q force q=p+k. Mod p, qr=-1, q=1 mod p would give k=1 with q=p+1 composite for odd p; qr cannot witness for odd p, so r=1 mod p and k=p-1, yielding q=2p-1 and r=2p+1. If p>3 one candidate multiple of 3 and >3. Thus p=3 gives 3,5,7; p=2 gives k=1, 2,3,5. Explicit witnesses 30: (3,10,6), 105:(7,21,15). For one or two primes a witness for largest prime is too small. Independent direct divisor-condition enumeration over all triples of the first 46 primes (15180 cases) reproduced exactly the two; this finite check is not the global proof.
residual_risks: This classifies a necessary numerical congruence, not finite simple groups or nonsquarefree/higher-support n.
